🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 13)
Channel: alert-system (+ alert-runtime-monitoring, alert-frontend-errors)  •  bug-type guess: env (memory exhaustion)  •  alerts in group: 5
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `DevOps` (`@devops` / `#team-devops`) for the hosts; `Integrations` (rest-api, Method.Data.RestApi); `Admin` (`@admin`) for gateway/auth

Symptoms:
  - *prod-msl-03 and prod-msl-04 are out of memory right now:* `system.mem.pct_usable` ~1–2% (was 16–17% on 11-12), `system.swap.pct_free` *0%* on both (was 99% on 11-11). prod-msl-05 is fine (61% usable, swap untouched, no rest-api).
  - *rest-api is the biggest growth:* `runtime.dotnet.mem.committed{service:rest-api}` went from ~2 GB to 8–11 GB per host in a step at *~11-18 18:00Z*. It hasn't come back down (msl-03 ≈8 GB, msl-04 ≈9–11 GB). events-subscribers-sync on msl-03 went from 0.55 to 1.55 GB.
  - *It already caused a stall today:* at 20:04:30Z msl-03's load went from 2 to *314* in 2 min and its request throughput dropped to ~0. Every co-hosted service stalled. Gateway p95 hit 10s, then *89.7s* at 20:06:10Z, with ~243 gateway 5xx between 20:05 and 20:07. The gateway marked `ms_authentication` *Unhealthy*. p95 also spiked on ms-authentication-api (74.5s), ms-tags-api (93.9s), ms-scheduler-api (100s), and mobile-notifications (75.6s). Recovered by ~20:08Z.
  - Side effects: mobile-notifications `RedisTimeoutException` (thread-pool starvation, not Valkey; Valkey p95 stayed <0.25s for other clients). Right after the stall (20:08–20:10Z) the SMS rate limiter rejected 864 requests for one key (account 119941), consistent with a backlog flush. The approutine SendSms failures were mostly account `docudavit4`.

Trace IDs: n/a (host-level). Sample gateway error: DownstreamHealthCheck TaskCanceledException, 20:04:52Z, linux-prod-3/4
Likely cause: rest-api's memory footprint on msl-03/04 jumped ~4–5x around 11-18 18Z and stayed there, exhausting RAM and swap on both hosts. Trigger not pinned: the request mix is similar before and after, but file downloads rose ~5x (34 → 186 per 6h), which fits buffering-in-memory. Unconfirmed.
Suggested next action: *recycle rest-api on prod-msl-03 and prod-msl-04* (or the hosts) before the next stall, then find what changed for rest-api around 11-18 18:00Z (deploy? new integration pulling files?). There's no host memory/swap monitor on prod-msl-*. Nothing paged at 1% usable / 0% swap.

Alerts explained by this (DD-scan-diff, Slack MCP unavailable, so no permalinks):
  • 70171778 Unexpected number of 5XX errors (20:12Z)  • 227940275 Redis Errors is High (20:13Z)
  • 301582337 ms-tags-api P95 (20:19Z)  • 302056407 mobile-notifications-api P95 (20:19Z)  • 77419271 XHR errors (20:26Z)

Root-cause analysis (queries run this cycle):
  • `avg:runtime.dotnet.mem.committed{service:rest-api,env:prod} by {host}` 11-15→now: msl-03 1.7→9.8 GB, msl-04 2.1→10.9 GB
  • `avg:system.swap.pct_free{host:prod-msl-0[3-5]} by {host}` daily min: msl-03 0.99 (11-11)→0.00, msl-04 0.99→0.00, msl-05 1.00
  • `avg:system.load.1{*} by {host}` 20:00–20:12Z: prod-msl-03 peak 313.9 @20:06:22Z (all other hosts <12)
  • `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:gateway}` 10s buckets: 89.7s @20:06:10Z, baseline 0.1–0.2s

Evidence (each backing query returned data this cycle):
  • DD metric: rest-api committed memory by host: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=runtime.dotnet.mem.committed&exp_scope=service%3Arest-api%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1794700800&end=1795126500
  • DD metric: prod-msl-03 load: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=system.load.1&exp_scope=host%3Aprod-msl-03&exp_agg=avg&start=1795116600&end=1795126500
  • DD metric: msl swap free: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=system.swap.pct_free&exp_scope=host%3Aprod-msl-03&exp_agg=avg&start=1793836800&end=1795126500
  • DD metric: gateway p95: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.duration&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Agateway&exp_agg=avg&start=1795118400&end=1795119240
  • Kibana: gateway errors 20:03-20:09Z: https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-19T20:03:30Z',to:'2026-11-19T20:09:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'level.keyword%3AError%20AND%20fields.dd_service.keyword%3Agateway'))

🗂️ *triage-bot backlog catch-up — 2026-09-24 → 2026-11-18 (56-day gap)*
The bot didn't poll for 56 days. This cycle diffed the Datadog monitor scan against the old cutoff. Caveat: it only sees each monitor's *latest* trigger, so earlier fires during the gap are invisible. 83 in-scope monitor transitions → 43 investigated groups. Older backlog fires are summarised here instead of posted one by one. Full detail is in docs/investigations/ and docs/actionable/2026-11-19.md.

*Real events worth a look:*
  1. *11-10 03:30–07:00Z: production SQL Server unreachable (~3.5h, Sun night ET).* ES SqlException counts: ~40/h baseline, 3,072 at 03:30–04:00Z, ≥10k/h 04:00–06:30Z, back to 9 by 07:00Z. `error 40 - Could not open a connection to SQL Server` on many hosts (ip-172-31-94-57, ip-172-31-120-89, PROD-UTILITY-02/03…). Error storm on recovery at 06:10–06:55Z: rest-api ≥10k, ms-authentication-api 6,060, oauth2 1,966, ms-account-api 1,536 (vs 186 total the next night). *Was this planned maintenance?* If so, nobody told the monitors. 9 alerts (approutine/runtime-core-subscriber 5xx, ms-tags 5xx, eda_inventory, ms-documents, EDA API) were its recovery tail. Kibana: https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-10T03:00:00Z',to:'2026-11-10T07:30:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.ExceptionDetail.Type.keyword%3A%22Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlException%22'))
  2. *11-13 17:37–22:15Z: Datadog APM went dark fleet-wide for ~4.6h during business hours.* Every prod host except prod-rt-01..04 stopped sending traces in the same 5-min bucket (Windows and Linux). ES shows the services kept serving (gateway logs 18–22Z: 2,946 vs 3,924 the day before). ~16 'no traffic / heartbeat silent' monitors flipped at 22:17–22:26Z when traces resumed, so false alarms. The real problem is 4.6h of APM blindness. Worth checking the DD agent / APM intake / API key for that window.
  3. *miurl + miurl-agent APM gone since ~10-20.* Hits went 12k/5d → 656 → nothing. 4 monitors are stuck in No Data. Decommissioned, migrated, or tracer lost? Owner `Transactions`.
  4. *reportgenerationapi heartbeat monitor blind since 11-05.* The service still serves ~29k req/day, but `/health/heartbeat` isn't being hit any more.
  5. *SendGrid bounce rate (314212200) fired again 11-13.* Still no KB entry; this is a known scoring gap.

*Monitor-hygiene notes:*
  • 17 'fires' were creation artifacts (`created == last_triggered_ts`): the 13-monitor [Valkey prod] suite (10-16), 3 nativemobile RUM monitors, and one Valkey dev monitor.
  • `[Valkey prod] Redis client errors by service` (333494099) shows *Alert* forever because its query lacks `default_zero()`. Groups for sync-xero-subscriber (04:01Z, Xero 429/500s) and mobile-notifications (17:31Z) can never resolve.

*Known-issue / false-alarm recurrences (backlog, logged and KB-bumped, not posted):* RTC p95 ×2 (11-15), ms-scheduler SeriesId -1 (11-16, 4 ES hits), runtime-core-subscriber quiet-period flap (11-18), EDA Kafka produce noise (10-11), methodportal apps low-traffic 5xx (11-04), push-registration (11-03), reportgen p95 (11-18), Twilio SMS warn threshold (11-18, monitor edited 8 min before fire).
*Low-impact needs-human (actionable.md only):* Valkey read-latency stall (10-19) and replication lag (10-20) not re-verified; ms-scheduler p95 100s (11-04); runtime-core p90 88s (11-12); nativemobile logout / Unable-to-Load / WebView-restore / crash monitors (11-13..11-19).
